ladders.title: The core loop
ladders.description: Dig down, haul ore home, sell it, buy a better pod, go deeper. Fuel is the clock and the deep hits back. This is the first pillar, the upgrade loop.

ladders.title: Money, fuel and spoil
ladders.description: Ore becomes money at the processor; money becomes parts, fuel and repairs. Rock the drill used to destroy becomes spoil, then slag brick, then new salvage crates.

ladders.title: The ore ladder
ladders.description: Seven ores, cheap to dear. All seven are in layer 1 and below, rarer in the deep zones. Cicatrium is the catalyst, not a sale.

ladders.title: Bootstrap: salvage to the first run
ladders.description: There is no tree and no ore on the surface. Salvage crates and fungal stalks give wood and metal; the metal builds the terminal parts; the terminals bring the colony back; the Mole goes down.

ladders.title: The colony's terminals
ladders.description: Each terminal is a Company machine, dead until its parts go in, and the repairs form a chain. One repair serves every charter in the world.

ladders.title: The Employee Handbook
ladders.description: Nine chapters of directives that tick off by themselves as you play, then Notes found in the world. It teaches the rules; the world stays a mystery.

ladders.title: Layers, breaches and the story
ladders.description: A chain of layers, each with three zones, joined by breach crusts. Layers 1 and 2 exist; the rest of the eight story layers, the Ramp and the uncharted worlds are planned.

ladders.title: Charters, crews and accounts
ladders.description: A charter is the crew's company: its own account, pods, parts and story. Friendly, never PvP.

ladders.title: The colony: Prosperity
ladders.description: A derelict Company mining town built once at the spawn, with a ring of salvage around it and the Conduit running down from it.

ladders.title: The pod chassis ladder
ladders.description: Each chassis is generally better than the one before but leans somewhere, so older ones keep a job. Each caps the tier of its parts.

ladders.title: Drill
ladders.description: Faster boring, from the stock tricone to the sixth tier. Each tier changes the cutter on the front.

ladders.title: Hull
ladders.description: More hull to take lava, gas, crust and hard landings.

ladders.title: Engine
ladders.description: More thrust for the rotor and treads.

ladders.title: Fuel tank
ladders.description: A bigger tank buys a longer dive.

ladders.title: Radiator
ladders.description: Cuts the heat the hull takes from lava; a vital part from the Magma Belt down.

ladders.title: Cargo bay
ladders.description: More ore slots, so more per trip.

ladders.title: Scanner
ladders.description: Range and what it can see: ore, then lava, then gas.

ladders.title: Lights
ladders.description: Pod lights are the only light below the surface; a brighter lamp lights more of the dark and keeps the Retained away.

ladders.title: Lava and its counters
ladders.description: Lava floods a bore through layer rock. The pod shields its pilot, so the hull is what lava costs. The ladder: see it, line the shaft by hand, line it automatically, hear it come, then shrug it off.

ladders.title: Gas and its counters
ladders.description: Gas pockets look like stone and blast the hull when the drill opens them; damage grows with depth. Steer round them, hear them, then bleed them.

ladders.title: Company Rock and its counters
ladders.description: Company Rock is a block in the layers that the drill refuses and a hand cannot break. A pilot can steer round it for free, or buy a blasting charge to clear it and keep a straight shaft; a shaped charge and a late drill tier are planned.

ladders.title: The Retained and other creatures
ladders.description: The Retained are tall, thin, lampless figures that come to dark pods and drain their fuel. They never attack. Lights keep them away, and a grab ends only when the figure is killed: by the pod's drill, or a sword on foot.

ladders.title: Darkness and sight
ladders.description: Below the surface there is no sky. An unlit cave is almost black, a stranded pod goes dark, and the Company's cheerful signs explain less the deeper you go.

ladders.title: The breach crust and hard landings
ladders.description: The hull is the pod's life. A fall, a crust and the layers' hazards all spend it; a pod with none left is a wreck.

ladders.title: Stranded, rescue and the way home
ladders.description: Fuel is the clock. Running dry strands the pod, and a pod with no hull is a wreck. Getting back up is staged: carried fuel, tow lines, emergency teleports, then outposts and pads.

ladders.title: The repair station's shelf
ladders.description: Single-use items bought at the repair station. Cheap tools first, then emergency ways home.

ladders.title: Crew roles and seats
ladders.description: The goal is crew, not passengers: each extra seat should have a real-time job that helps, and a pilot can do a weaker version alone. Passengers are allowed until the jobs exist. Provisional until a playtest.

ladders.title: Cockpit, screens and HUD
ladders.description: Everything the player reads: the pod's gauges, the scanner map, the green-screen terminals, the handbook. All of it is resource-pack data, so a pack can restyle it.

ladders.title: Look and sound
ladders.description: Prosperity at dusk: a rust-red world under a slow dusk, 16 pixel textures drawn from recipes, GeckoLib pods and placeholder sound.

nodes.title: Start in Prosperity
nodes.summary: You spawn in a run-down Company mining town on a bare red plain, with a dead pod in the hangar.

nodes.title: Get a pod running
nodes.summary: Gather salvage, repair the terminals and the founding Mole.

nodes.title: Drive and drill down
nodes.summary: Treads on the ground, a rotor to fly, a drill that bores down and sideways, never up.

nodes.title: Fuel is the clock
nodes.summary: Fuel drains all the time and faster when drilling; running dry strands the pod.

nodes.title: Scan for ore
nodes.summary: The scanner is a side-view map of the rock around the pod, ore as bright dots.

nodes.title: Haul ore in the cargo bay
nodes.summary: Ore is heavy and non-stacking; a full bay cuts the lift.

nodes.title: Fly home
nodes.summary: Drive or fly back up the shaft before the fuel runs out.

nodes.title: Sell at the ore processor
nodes.summary: Park by the processor; the ore pays into the charter's account.

nodes.title: Buy better parts
nodes.summary: Money buys tiered pod parts at the upgrade terminal.

nodes.title: Go deeper
nodes.summary: A stronger pod bores through the breach into the next layer, where the ore pays more and the hazards bite harder.

nodes.title: The deep fights back
nodes.summary: Lava, gas, Company Rock, the crust, darkness and the Retained, each with a ladder of counters.

nodes.title: Ore in the cargo bay
nodes.summary: Mined ore rides home as heavy items; only our ore counts as cargo.

nodes.title: Sell ore for money
nodes.summary: The processor pays a fixed base price per ore.

nodes.title: Spoil
nodes.summary: With a spoil hopper the drill keeps one spoil for each block of waste rock; the bay holds 64.

nodes.title: Work orders
nodes.summary: The Company posts orders (deliver 10 bronzium) that pay a bonus and move the story; later ones repeat.

nodes.title: The charter's account
nodes.summary: One shared pot of money for the whole crew.

nodes.title: Press spoil into salvage crates
nodes.summary: The processor presses spoil into new salvage crates, so wood and scrap renew.

nodes.title: Slag brick
nodes.summary: The processor fuses 2 spoil into 1 brick for no money; bricks line shafts against lava.

nodes.title: Buy repairs and consumables
nodes.summary: Hull nanobots, dynamite, explosives, teleport items and a reserve tank at the repair station.

nodes.title: Buy fuel at the pump
nodes.summary: Early fuel is crafted; later it is bought at the fuel pump.

nodes.title: Buy pod parts
nodes.summary: Tier 2 and up of drill, hull, engine, tank, radiator, cargo and scanner, and every tier of lights and the hazard answers. Tier 1 of the first seven is crafted.

nodes.title: Catalysts
nodes.summary: Every chassis and every couple of tiers also needs a rare material from one layer; Cicatrium is the first.

nodes.title: Records board
nodes.summary: One entry per charter at the colony: deepest breach, wealth hauled, wrecks salvaged.

nodes.title: Registration fees grow
nodes.summary: Each extra pod a charter registers costs more, so a free second Mole is no cheap deep miner.

nodes.title: Ironium
nodes.summary: $30 an ore. Many small brown chunks. The baseline.

nodes.title: Bronzium
nodes.summary: $60 an ore. Two fat orange domes.

nodes.title: Silverium
nodes.summary: $100 an ore. A thin thread with two pale crystals.

nodes.title: Goldium
nodes.summary: $250 an ore. A thread that swells into one bright nugget.

nodes.title: Platinium
nodes.summary: $750 an ore. Two thick lilac-white bars.

nodes.title: Einsteinium
nodes.summary: $2000 an ore. Two teal crystals in dark hollows.

nodes.title: Cicatrium
nodes.summary: $1500 an ore. A red scar with a wound in it. The catalyst for chassis restores; it is not sold.

nodes.title: Fungal stalks
nodes.summary: Pale stalks on crater floors are the wood: press to planks, burn for heat, char to charcoal.

nodes.title: Salvage crates
nodes.summary: Company crates in a ring 100 to 160 blocks out; break one for planks, sticks, cloth, scrap and redstone.

nodes.title: Salvage cloth
nodes.summary: Cloth from a crate; it crafts into string.

nodes.title: Scrap iron and copper
nodes.summary: The crate's metal; melted one for one in a furnace.

nodes.title: Melt scrap in a furnace
nodes.summary: Planks burn to melt scrap into iron and copper ingots.

nodes.title: Tools, a table and a torch
nodes.summary: Handbook chapter 1: craft stone tools, then a first light.

nodes.title: Craft the terminal parts
nodes.summary: Ten crafted parts, from iron, copper and redstone, repair the four colony terminals.

nodes.title: Repair the terminals in order
nodes.summary: Pump, processor, upgrade terminal, repair station, each once per world.

nodes.title: Craft the Mole's parts
nodes.summary: A drill head, a fuel injector, a rotor hub and a tread assembly bring the founding Mole back.

nodes.title: Craft the first scanner
nodes.summary: Craft a scanner unit from 4 iron, 2 copper and 2 redstone and use it on your pod: that fits the tier 1 scanner. The terminal does not sell tier 1.

nodes.title: Craft the first-tier parts
nodes.summary: Craft a drill, hull, engine, fuel tank, radiator or cargo bay unit from salvage iron, copper and redstone and use it on your pod: that fits the tier 1 part. The terminal does not sell tier 1; tier 2 and up are purchases.

nodes.title: Repair the founding Mole
nodes.summary: The first charter fixes the hangar's Mole; the Company advances the pod.

nodes.title: The first run
nodes.summary: Refuel, scan, drill layer 1, sell, buy a first part.

nodes.title: Contract terminal
nodes.summary: Works from the start: found a charter or sign on as crew.

nodes.title: Fuel pump
nodes.summary: Sells fuel to a parked pod. The first repair.

nodes.title: Ore processor
nodes.summary: Buys ore, fuses slag brick, presses crates, lists work orders.

nodes.title: Upgrade terminal
nodes.summary: Sells tiered pod parts.

nodes.title: Repair station
nodes.summary: Mends the hull and sells consumables.

nodes.title: Hangar console
nodes.summary: Founds the Mole, restores wrecks into pods and buys a refurbished Mole for later charters.

nodes.title: Parked pod uses the terminal
nodes.summary: Park a pod beside a terminal and it works on the pod, not on the player.

nodes.title: Outpost terminals
nodes.summary: Fuel and sell terminals built at depth, selling at worse rates than the colony.

nodes.title: The handbook item
nodes.summary: Issued when you sign your contract, bound to you, opened with H.

nodes.title: 1. Welcome to Prosperity
nodes.summary: Gather wood, craft tools, gather scrap, smelt iron, craft a scanner unit.

nodes.title: 2. Bringing Prosperity Back Online
nodes.summary: Repair the pump, the processor and the upgrade terminal.

nodes.title: 3. Meet the Mole
nodes.summary: Repair the Mole and board it.

nodes.title: 4. Fuel Is Life
nodes.summary: Refuel, fly, drill down and return to the colony.

nodes.title: 5. Every Sale Counts
nodes.summary: Sell ore, buy a component, install it.

nodes.title: 6. Seeing Below
nodes.summary: Install the scanner and find ore with it.

nodes.title: Hazards on higher scanners
nodes.summary: A handbook line about unseen hazards that a thermal tier shows; its wording is a user pick.

nodes.title: 7. Staying Safe on the Claim
nodes.summary: Repair the hull and reach the Deep Claim.

nodes.title: 8. Your First Breach
nodes.summary: Break through the crust into layer 2.

nodes.title: 9. Recovering Company Property
nodes.summary: Find the Prospector wreck, tow it, restore it, reach layer 2's floor.

nodes.title: Notes
nodes.summary: Miners' scribbles, torn pages and wreck logs found in the world; one found by anyone fills every member's handbook.

nodes.title: Revisions
nodes.summary: The handbook is revised five times as the story turns; tone changes, rules never do.

nodes.title: Spec sheets and first-exposure warnings
nodes.summary: After layer 2, each new rule is explained when you first meet it, not by a chapter.

nodes.title: The surface
nodes.summary: Regolith plains, craters and terraced mesas under a dusk sky that never reaches day. No ore, no trees.

nodes.title: Layer 1: The Claim
nodes.summary: Dirt and stone, the first ores and the previous miners' shafts. Teaches the loop.

nodes.title: Topsoil Claims
nodes.summary: The top third of layer 1.

nodes.title: Stone Benches
nodes.summary: The middle third of layer 1.

nodes.title: Deep Claim
nodes.summary: The bottom third of layer 1, where lava starts.

nodes.title: Structures in the layers
nodes.summary: Shafts with Note niches, a punch clock, a gallery with a quota board, rails and timbering, and wreck sites.

nodes.title: The first breach
nodes.summary: A crust at the layer's floor: any drill gets through, slowly, hot and hurt. A rumble and a transmission mark the crossing.

nodes.title: Deepest point
nodes.summary: A charter's deepest point sets which orders and transmissions open.

nodes.title: Transmissions
nodes.summary: The story arrives as green-screen messages that fire once per charter, mostly at its deepest point.

nodes.title: Layer 2: The Old Workings
nodes.summary: Collapsed mine levels, rails, a salvageable Prospector wreck, garbled transmissions.

nodes.title: Layer rock textures and grades
nodes.summary: Grained rock textures for layers 1 and 2, a lava redraw and an I-beam fix; depth palettes and colour grades follow.

nodes.title: Upper Levels
nodes.summary: The top third of layer 2.

nodes.title: Shift Change
nodes.summary: The middle third of layer 2, where Cicatrium first appears.

nodes.title: Prospector's Run
nodes.summary: The bottom third of layer 2, with the Prospector wreck.

nodes.title: Breach crossing with no teleport
nodes.summary: Crossing a breach inside the campaign world is a pure dig, with a rumble and a transmission.

nodes.title: One tall campaign world
nodes.summary: The surface and story layers share one dimension, each a Y band with its own light and fog.

nodes.title: Layer 3: Fungal Hollows
nodes.summary: Huge fungal caverns lit by their own glow, spore gas, the first real on-foot exploring.

nodes.title: Layer 4: The Drowned Deep
nodes.summary: Flooded caverns and pressure; the pod needs seals. The lost miners' story plays out.

nodes.title: Layers 5 to 8
nodes.summary: The Lattice, the Magma Belt, the Ossuary and the Furnace, ending at Head Office.

nodes.title: The finale: a choice
nodes.summary: The boss breaks but cannot die; renounce the Controlling Interest to win, or sign and become the Chairman.

nodes.title: The Ramp
nodes.summary: A few hundred blocks where drilling gets exponentially harder; the end of the campaign is obvious.

nodes.title: Seams and the grained crust
nodes.summary: A fast background swap hidden in a vertical-grained crust, with decoys that look the same.

nodes.title: Story-layer splicing
nodes.summary: An update adds a new story layer at the seam without touching what is built ('the depths moved').

nodes.title: Uncharted layers
nodes.summary: Endless 2048-tall worlds below the ramp, a bragging-rights grind for the records board.

nodes.title: Found a charter
nodes.summary: Name it at the contract terminal and become its Director; it gets an account.

nodes.title: Parts are company property
nodes.summary: Parts are bound to the charter and serial-numbered; another charter's parts are void.

nodes.title: Sign on as crew
nodes.summary: Apply with an Employment Contract; the Director approves.

nodes.title: Dormant charters
nodes.summary: A charter nobody belongs to goes dormant and keeps its name, account and pods; its former members can revive it.

nodes.title: Serial numbers
nodes.summary: Each pod and part has a world-wide serial; a restored wreck keeps its own number.

nodes.title: Revive at the contract terminal
nodes.summary: The contract terminal lists the dormant charters you once belonged to; REVIVE makes you its Director. Strangers are refused.

nodes.title: A restored wreck keeps its serial
nodes.summary: The famous wreck carries a lore mark and keeps PROSPECTOR-0002 and its name tag when restored; a charter's own Prospectors skip 0002.

nodes.title: Outposts and pads shared
nodes.summary: A toggle to share a charter's outposts and pads with other charters.

nodes.title: Competition between charters
nodes.summary: A later update might add rivalry; today charters are friendly.

nodes.title: The square and the Host
nodes.summary: The Host's statue stands ten blocks tall in the middle of the Pithead Works.

nodes.title: Chapel, bunkhouse and the Lamp and Pick
nodes.summary: The quiet corners of town, with signs and notes.

nodes.title: The hangar
nodes.summary: Holds the founding pod, dark until your charter repairs it.

nodes.title: Offices and the Works
nodes.summary: The pay office, Personnel, the Continuity Office, the ore house and the headframe.

nodes.title: The statue's hands
nodes.summary: A work order puts the Host's hands back.

nodes.title: Company lamps
nodes.summary: The Company's caged sodium lamp, lit or dark; placed by the colony.

nodes.title: The Conduit
nodes.summary: An undiggable Company pipe from the ore processor straight down through every layer to the Furnace. The story's first clue.

nodes.title: The colony kit
nodes.summary: 24 Company building blocks (plates, beams, pipes, rails, signs, windows) the town is built from; unbreakable.

nodes.title: Anchor mode and outposts
nodes.summary: A Behemoth that unfolds into a temporary outpost; built outposts with beds and storage.

nodes.title: Mole
nodes.summary: The founding pod: 1 seat, parts up to tier 2, built for layers 1 and 2. 2 blocks wide and 3 tall.

nodes.title: Pod looks
nodes.summary: A GeckoLib model per chassis; the drill tier picks the cutter on the front.

nodes.title: Charter paint
nodes.summary: Pods are painted per charter and the rotor folds out to fly.

nodes.title: Prospector
nodes.summary: A wreck from layer 2: 2 seats, parts up to tier 3, up to layer 3.

nodes.title: Restore a wreck into a pod
nodes.summary: Tow a wreck home and pay money plus catalysts at the hangar console.

nodes.title: Badger
nodes.summary: A wreck from layer 3 or 4: 2 to 3 seats, adds the operator, leans to the drill.

nodes.title: Bore scales with the chassis
nodes.summary: A bigger pod carves a bigger tunnel, so its cab and bore grow together.

nodes.title: Hauler
nodes.summary: A wreck from layer 4 or 5: 3 seats, leans to cargo. Later the tender pod.

nodes.title: Crawler
nodes.summary: A wreck from layer 6: 3 to 4 seats, leans to armour against heat and pressure.

nodes.title: Behemoth
nodes.summary: A wreck from layer 7: 4 to 6 seats and an anchor mode.

nodes.title: Drill: stock
nodes.summary: The stock tricone cutter. Speed 1x.

nodes.title: Drill tier 1
nodes.summary: Drill speed 1.4x stock. Crafted as a drill unit and fitted by use, never sold at the terminal. A Mole fits it.

nodes.title: Drill tier 2
nodes.summary: Stacked rings on the cutter, $500. The best a Mole takes.

nodes.title: Drill tier 3
nodes.summary: Drill speed 2.5x stock, $1,250. The best a Prospector takes.

nodes.title: Drill tier 4
nodes.summary: Drill speed 3.5x stock, $5,000. No chassis built yet can fit it (a Badger or later).

nodes.title: Drill tier 5
nodes.summary: Drill speed 4.75x stock, $25,000. No chassis built yet can fit it (a Badger or later).

nodes.title: Drill tier 6
nodes.summary: Drill speed 6.0x stock, $125,000. No chassis built yet can fit it (a Badger or later).

nodes.title: Hull: stock
nodes.summary: The stock hull. 1x.

nodes.title: Hull tier 1
nodes.summary: Hull 1.7x stock. Crafted as a hull unit and fitted by use, never sold at the terminal. A Mole fits it.

nodes.title: Hull tier 2
nodes.summary: Hull 3.0x stock, $500. The best a Mole takes.

nodes.title: Hull tier 3
nodes.summary: Hull 5.0x stock, $1,250. The best a Prospector takes.

nodes.title: Hull tier 4
nodes.summary: Hull 8.0x stock, $5,000. No chassis built yet can fit it (a Badger or later).

nodes.title: Hull tier 5
nodes.summary: Hull 12.0x stock, $25,000. No chassis built yet can fit it (a Badger or later).

nodes.title: Hull tier 6
nodes.summary: Hull 18.0x stock, $125,000. No chassis built yet can fit it (a Badger or later).

nodes.title: Engine: stock
nodes.summary: The stock engine. 1x.

nodes.title: Engine tier 1
nodes.summary: Engine 1.07x stock. Crafted as an engine unit and fitted by use, never sold at the terminal. A Mole fits it.

nodes.title: Engine tier 2
nodes.summary: Engine 1.13x stock, $500. The best a Mole takes.

nodes.title: Engine tier 3
nodes.summary: Engine 1.2x stock, $1,250. The best a Prospector takes.

nodes.title: Engine tier 4
nodes.summary: Engine 1.27x stock, $5,000. No chassis built yet can fit it (a Badger or later).

nodes.title: Engine tier 5
nodes.summary: Engine 1.33x stock, $25,000. No chassis built yet can fit it (a Badger or later).

nodes.title: Engine tier 6
nodes.summary: Engine 1.4x stock, $125,000. No chassis built yet can fit it (a Badger or later).

nodes.title: Fuel tank: stock
nodes.summary: The stock 10 litre tank.

nodes.title: Fuel tank tier 1
nodes.summary: Tank 1.5x stock. Crafted as a fuel tank unit and fitted by use, never sold at the terminal. A Mole fits it.

nodes.title: Fuel tank tier 2
nodes.summary: Tank 2.5x stock, $500. The best a Mole takes.

nodes.title: Fuel tank tier 3
nodes.summary: Tank 4.0x stock, $1,250. The best a Prospector takes.

nodes.title: Fuel tank tier 4
nodes.summary: Tank 6.0x stock, $5,000. No chassis built yet can fit it (a Badger or later).

nodes.title: Fuel tank tier 5
nodes.summary: Tank 10.0x stock, $25,000. No chassis built yet can fit it (a Badger or later).

nodes.title: Fuel tank tier 6
nodes.summary: Tank 15.0x stock, $125,000. No chassis built yet can fit it (a Badger or later).

nodes.title: Radiator: stock
nodes.summary: The stock radiator. Takes all the heat.

nodes.title: Radiator tier 1
nodes.summary: Lava costs 90 percent of stock. Crafted as a radiator unit and fitted by use, never sold at the terminal. A Mole fits it.

nodes.title: Radiator tier 2
nodes.summary: Lava costs 75 percent of stock, $1,250. The best a Mole takes.

nodes.title: Radiator tier 3
nodes.summary: Lava costs 60 percent of stock, $5,000. The best a Prospector takes.

nodes.title: Radiator tier 4
nodes.summary: Lava costs 40 percent of stock, $25,000. No chassis built yet can fit it (a Badger or later).

nodes.title: Radiator tier 5
nodes.summary: Lava costs 20 percent of stock, $125,000. No chassis built yet can fit it (a Badger or later).

nodes.title: Cargo bay: stock
nodes.summary: The stock bay, 7 ore slots.

nodes.title: Cargo bay tier 1
nodes.summary: 15 ore slots. Crafted as a cargo bay unit and fitted by use, never sold at the terminal. A Mole fits it.

nodes.title: Cargo bay tier 2
nodes.summary: 25 ore slots, $500. The best a Mole takes.

nodes.title: Cargo bay tier 3
nodes.summary: 40 ore slots, $1,250. The best a Prospector takes.

nodes.title: Cargo bay tier 4
nodes.summary: 70 ore slots, $5,000. No chassis built yet can fit it (a Badger or later).

nodes.title: Cargo bay tier 5
nodes.summary: 120 ore slots, $25,000. No chassis built yet can fit it (a Badger or later).

nodes.title: Scanner tier 1
nodes.summary: The first map: ore in range. Crafted as a scanner unit and fitted by use, never sold at the terminal; every later tier is a purchase. A Mole fits it.

nodes.title: Scanner tier 2
nodes.summary: The thermal tier: lava shows bright red, lava in the wall dim red. $500, and tier 1 must be fitted first. The best a Mole takes.

nodes.title: Scanner tier 3
nodes.summary: Gas pockets show on the map. $1,250. The Prospector's tier. The best a Prospector takes.

nodes.title: Scanner tier 4
nodes.summary: The widest, clearest map. $5,000. No chassis built yet can fit it (a Badger or later).

nodes.title: Lights tier 1
nodes.summary: A first lamp, light level 6, $125. Lit pods draw no Retained. A Mole fits it.

nodes.title: Lights tier 2
nodes.summary: Light level 9, $375. The best a Mole takes.

nodes.title: Lights tier 3
nodes.summary: Light level 12, $1,250. The best a Prospector takes.

nodes.title: Lights tier 4
nodes.summary: Light level 15, $3,750. No chassis built yet can fit it (a Badger or later).

nodes.title: Lava in the rock
nodes.summary: Pockets of lava from the Deep Claim down; a bore opens the cells beside it and the lava runs in.

nodes.title: The pod shields its pilot
nodes.summary: A seated pilot takes no lava damage; the hull burns instead, 10 a second, with a HULL BURNING readout and a hiss.

nodes.title: Spoil hopper
nodes.summary: The 'keep stone' part: the drill keeps spoil for bricks instead of destroying it. $100.

nodes.title: Hand lining
nodes.summary: Press R from the seat and the pod lays slag brick round the slab while it stands still.

nodes.title: Liner tier 1
nodes.summary: Lines the shaft with brick as the pod drills, every 4 slabs, only where lava can reach. $500.

nodes.title: Liner tier 2
nodes.summary: Rings every 3 slabs, also in a fall, and each brick lines more. $1,000. The best a Mole takes.

nodes.title: The lava watch
nodes.summary: A HUD line and lamp when flowing lava closes on the pod from behind; every pod has it, free.

nodes.title: Heat shield
nodes.summary: A one-tier part, $750. While lava touches the pod, burning slag bricks soak its damage at 4 hull a brick, from the rack first and then the pilot's pack. The HUD shows GLAZE HOLDING or GLAZE SPENT.

nodes.title: Gas pockets
nodes.summary: A pocket that looks like plain stone and blasts the hull when bored; the biggest cause of deaths in layer 1.

nodes.title: Dynamite on a slab
nodes.summary: Blast a pocket from a distance, if you know where it is. Costly.

nodes.title: Seep sounder tier 1
nodes.summary: A SEEPAGE readout counts the slabs down to a pocket and a hiss quickens as the drill nears. $400.

nodes.title: Seep sounder tier 2
nodes.summary: Reaches 4 slabs down and 2 blocks to each side, and bleeds a marked pocket before boring it. $1,000.

nodes.title: Sideways bores spread the blast
nodes.summary: A pod that opens a pocket sideways takes only a share of the blast, per cell of its slab.

nodes.title: Gas on the map
nodes.summary: Scanner tier 3, on the Prospector, draws pockets in its slice; the sounder stays the cheap Mole part.

nodes.title: Company Rock
nodes.summary: Rock the drill refuses. Steer round it (fuel, time, the next pocket) or blast it with a charge to keep the shaft straight.

nodes.title: Company Rock look
nodes.summary: A concept round for how Company Rock looks is under way; the chosen look is built later.

nodes.title: Steer round it
nodes.summary: Step the pod aside and drill on; the scanner shows nothing of it.

nodes.title: Blasting charge
nodes.summary: A $40 charge set from the seat under the pod. After a 3 second fuse it clears Company Rock and the rock round it, and hurts a pod that stays within 3 blocks. About 5 a straight layer 1 shaft.

nodes.title: Shaped charge
nodes.summary: A dearer, directed blast that clears a whole slab column.

nodes.title: A drill tier that bites Company Rock
nodes.summary: A late drill that cuts it slowly at a cost in heat and fuel, so charges keep a niche.

nodes.title: The Retained
nodes.summary: A lampless figure in the open dark of layers 1 and 2, drawn to pods with no lights; about a third carry a small lamp. It never attacks and never speaks.

nodes.title: The grab and the drain
nodes.summary: It walks to a pod within 20 blocks, clings to the hull and drains fuel, never below 5 percent. The grip ends only when the figure dies.

nodes.title: Lights keep them away
nodes.summary: A pod with a lights part draws no Retained. Lights do not free a pod that is already held.

nodes.title: Kill it with the drill
nodes.summary: No fading: a grab ends only when the Retained dies. The cutter bites it while the pod drills rock, and a sword kills it on foot.

nodes.title: More common deep, facing the pod, a helmet lens
nodes.summary: Layer 1 rolls 1 percent and layer 2 5 percent, up to 5 at once; a figure faces the pod it grips; a tiny dim amber lens shines in its helmet.

nodes.title: Creatures and combat session
nodes.summary: A session with the user on rare unsettling creatures per layer and bosses; pod combat uses mining gear first.

nodes.title: Layer bosses
nodes.summary: Bosses that mix pod fights and on-foot fights, by layer.

nodes.title: The Chairman
nodes.summary: The two-phase finale boss, broken but never killed.

nodes.title: Darkness
nodes.summary: Each layer sets its own ambient light, darker with depth. Pod lights are the only light you have.

nodes.title: Pod light ledger
nodes.summary: A pod's light blocks are recorded in a ledger before they are placed, so they move with the pod and clear when it leaves.

nodes.title: A stranded pod goes dark
nodes.summary: With no fuel or hull the pod is powered off, and its lights go out.

nodes.title: Smooth moving light
nodes.summary: Glow accents, beams, an optional dynamic-lights mod and an opt-in shader pack.

nodes.title: The suit lamp
nodes.summary: On foot, a suit lamp on a battery; the finale's Unnumbered Lamp never runs out.

nodes.title: HUD signal decay
nodes.summary: Near the bottom of a layer the readouts flicker, jump and finally drop out; the deeper, the more often.

nodes.title: Console upgrade
nodes.summary: A cockpit track whose tiers push the decay deeper; the top tier is immune.

nodes.title: Per-layer drones and the Lamp Hymn
nodes.summary: Each layer gets its own sound drone, with a hymn motif.

nodes.title: Hard landings
nodes.summary: The hull takes damage from the sink speed at landing; a pilot who taps the rotor lands unhurt from any height.

nodes.title: Brake with the rotor
nodes.summary: Holding the sink speed under 14 blocks a second costs fuel and saves the hull.

nodes.title: The breach crust
nodes.summary: Three rows of hard rock at each layer floor: 8 hull a row, 24 in all, and heat.

nodes.title: Crust warning
nodes.summary: An amber line within 16 slabs of the crust says how much hull you have and what it will take.

nodes.title: Breach brace
nodes.summary: At rest above the crust the brace burns the cheapest ore to patch hull. $200. Fits every chassis.

nodes.title: Earthquakes and cave-ins
nodes.summary: In certain layers a quake or cave-in blocks a stretch of shaft, small or large; it never deletes built blocks.

nodes.title: Clearing a blockage
nodes.summary: Explosives on foot, a pod charge launcher, crewmates from above, or an emergency teleport.

nodes.title: Heat, pressure and flooding
nodes.summary: Later layers add heat (the Magma Belt), pressure and flooding (the Drowned Deep) that the hull and radiator must answer.

nodes.title: Stranded
nodes.summary: Out of fuel, the pod is powered off and dark until rescue or a reserve tank.

nodes.title: Refuel by hand
nodes.summary: Right-click the pod with coal, charcoal or biofuel; 2 litres each.

nodes.title: Reserve tank
nodes.summary: A tank crafted from iron and a bucket that restarts a stranded pod.

nodes.title: The tow line
nodes.summary: Hold a tow cable and right-click another pod; the towed pod hangs below and behind on a 5 block line, across breaches.

nodes.title: Wrecks
nodes.summary: A pod with no hull goes dark where it fell, with its cargo, and its owners are told.

nodes.title: A chain, not smoke
nodes.summary: The tow line is a real chain of links on a sagging curve: it hangs when slack, goes straight when pulled, and shows in the dark of a layer.

nodes.title: Wrecked prefabs that drop salvage
nodes.summary: Ruined buildings and vehicles in the world that give scrap when broken.

nodes.title: Outposts at depth
nodes.summary: Built shelters with fuel and sell terminals, beds and storage; the first goes at the layer 1 floor.

nodes.title: Environment ratings
nodes.summary: Each depth rates heat, pressure, flooding and quakes; an outpost under the rating is uninhabitable but never destroyed.

nodes.title: Teleport pads
nodes.summary: Paired pads a charter builds, at a power cost that grows with depth and mass; nothing mined teleports.

nodes.title: Anchor mode
nodes.summary: A parked Behemoth unfolds into a walkable temporary outpost.

nodes.title: Dynamite
nodes.summary: A 3 by 3 blast for a blocked shaft or a known gas pocket. $100.

nodes.title: Reserve fuel tank
nodes.summary: A bought reserve tank that restarts a stranded pod. $100.

nodes.title: Hull repair nanobots
nodes.summary: Patches the hull. $345.

nodes.title: Plastic explosives
nodes.summary: A 5 by 5 blast. $300.

nodes.title: Quantum teleporter
nodes.summary: Sends you to the nearest pad or the surface; you drop your cargo. $690.

nodes.title: Matter transmitter
nodes.summary: A dearer way home, with the same drop. $1,390.

nodes.title: Pilot
nodes.summary: The legs: movement, flight, fuel.

nodes.title: Passengers
nodes.summary: A seat with no job is allowed: the Prospector's second seat carries a passenger until the navigator's sonar exists.

nodes.title: Navigator
nodes.summary: The eyes: active sonar, pings that cost power, echoes that must be read, targets marked on the pilot's HUD.

nodes.title: Operator
nodes.summary: The hands: a manipulator arm and a charge launcher; a turret later.

nodes.title: Robots fill empty seats
nodes.summary: A component that fills the navigator or operator seat with less skill.

nodes.title: Tender runs and spotting
nodes.summary: One pod brings fuel and empty bays to a pod that keeps drilling; a second pod scans ahead.

nodes.title: Altimeter
nodes.summary: Depth in feet, computed from the layer offset plus local height; each layer has its own trick.

nodes.title: Pod status readout
nodes.summary: Hull, fuel and cargo in the corner, with warning lines (HULL BURNING, SEEPAGE, CRUST).

nodes.title: Account readout
nodes.summary: The charter's money, shown on the HUD.

nodes.title: Scanner map
nodes.summary: A side-view slice with ore, lava and gas in their own colours.

nodes.title: Breach fade
nodes.summary: The screen fades as the pod crosses a breach.

nodes.title: Transmission overlay
nodes.summary: Employer messages on a green CRT screen that types out its text.

nodes.title: Green-screen terminal panels
nodes.summary: Every terminal is a Hatch machine panel: a green screen in a riveted frame with a status strip.

nodes.title: Skins
nodes.summary: Colours, sizes and timings are theme data; a resource pack restyles them with F3+T.

nodes.title: Cockpit HUD with gauges
nodes.summary: A cockpit HUD with gauges that hides the vanilla hotbar while seated.

nodes.title: Front camera
nodes.summary: A part that turns the cab window into a video feed, clear to the edges, that lava can cook and static can cut.

nodes.title: A dusk sky that never reaches day
nodes.summary: A visual timeline sky swinging between dusk and deep night.

nodes.title: Textures from recipes
nodes.summary: Every 16 pixel texture is generated from data by tools/textures; no hand-painted files to drift.

nodes.title: Placeholder sound
nodes.summary: 47 sound events, all vanilla stand-ins; a private audio pack carries the original sounds for friends.

nodes.title: Lighting art
nodes.summary: Glow accents and beams; see Darkness and sight.

nodes.title: Salvage looks
nodes.summary: The salvage crate is the freight crate, with the low sled crate as an alternative resource pack; the fungal stalk is the shelf fungus. The other looks are gone.

nodes.title: A public release
nodes.summary: A name, a licence and a soundtrack the project may publish; Modrinth, with its AI-content disclosure.
